title: Newsletter Shutdown Looms!
subtitle: With the word-limit funding deal , the risk has come home to roost.
body_html:
In yesterday’s newsletter, we previewed the crisis for this newsletter, as a compromise on a Continuing Resolution to supply enough additional words for a “word-based” newsletter seems increasingly unlikely. Blog posts (pre-written) educating us about “what is treatment resistant depression” will run dry soon, I’m sure.

Both sides have, reportedly, dug in.

House Speaker Marky Mark said that his former allies knowns as The Funky Bunch “refuse to acknowledge the simple facts.” Senate Majority Leader accused the other side of “hostage-taking” and “hijacking” the word appropriations process. The Funpublican leaders said less fun senators should support a House-passed bill to extend funding. “They need to realize that, without nouns and verbs, this newsletter will cease to be relevant to the American people.”

While minority leadership in da house responded in a manner typically limp:

“We are a no when it comes to kicking the can down the road,” he said. “This issue needs to be dealt with immediately.”

Which, of course, is the opposite of what is happening.

As threatened, the publication might end up being a series of pictures. Today, on the eve of a complete shutdown of this newsletter, we present some pictures and music as a retrospective of what we can show— and allow you to hear—as we run out of words with which we can have things to say—it’s a cautionary tale, and a reminder of what’s to come.

None of these photos will come with an explanation or caption. Absent a Continuing Resolution, it’s just not possible to round up enough words. You will have to guess what these photos depict— and why they are even here! They share one quality: I took them all.

Let’s hope there is some compromise that breaks the word-block—this is going to be difficult to do with photos only. We may need to move to airline-style cartoons or other figurative renderings to make it all make sense.
